    AI Overview
    Xanax (alprazolam) is a benzodiazepine used for short-term treatment of anxiety disorders and panic disorders. It works by enhancing neurotransmitter activity to produce a calming effect. Common side effects include drowsiness and lightheadedness. It carries high risks of addiction, dependency, and severe withdrawal symptoms. 
    Key Information 
    • What it's for: Xanax treats anxiety, generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and panic disorders.
    • How it works: It acts on the brain and central nervous system, creating a calming effect.
    • Common side effects: Drowsiness, fatigue, memory issues, impaired coordination, and dizziness.
    • Withdrawal Symptoms: Stopping abruptly can cause serious withdrawal, including seizures, tremors, insomnia, vomiting, and sweating.
    • Interactions: Combining Xanax with alcohol or opioids is highly dangerous and can lead to severe sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death.
    • Safety Notice (April 2026): A nationwide recall has been issued for certain Viatris Xanax XR tablets (lot 8177156) due to failed quality control tests. 
    Important Safety Warnings 
    • Misuse/Addiction: It is a controlled substance with a high potential for abuse.
    • Dependence: Physical dependence can occur even with short-term use.
    • Do not mix: Never combine with alcohol or opioids. 
    Disclaimer: This is a summary. Always consult a healthcare provider for medical advice.
